rationale: boundary_events.json requires delivery of event_i assertions as short as 2 ns, and p1 samples it directly every 10 ns (line 8), so a permitted pulse between clk_b edges is lost. An Icarus witness confirms it: in the frozen bench, p1 and event_o never rise. CDC-013(c) diagnoses it, with a full p1->p2 chain, async launch event_src, and an observable event_o. Caveat: the SDC attaches create_clock event_src to the port event_i itself instead of a virtual clock. This declares event_i an SDC clock root with a 10 ns waveform, which contradicts the 2 ns contract and may cause side findings or limit the (c) proof. The boundary contract, not the clock period, is authoritative for duration. Raw rst_n release, recovery/removal and physical timing remain external obligations outside this label.
